data.body_html:
Estepona's coastline is one of the best places on the Costa del Sol for dolphin watching. With calm Mediterranean waters and a rich marine ecosystem, an Estepona boat charter dolphin watching season runs from May through September, when sighting rates regularly top 90%. Whether you're aboard a speedy 7-metre runabout or a 29-metre flybridge, the experience is unforgettable. This guide covers the best months, practical tips, and which boats from our fleet suit your group.

When Is Dolphin Season in Estepona?

The prime window runs from May to September, peaking in July and August when sea temperatures hit 24–26°C and baitfish are plentiful. Sighting rates in these months often exceed 95%. April and October can also yield good results, though success rates drop to 60–70% due to choppier seas and cooler water. Winter charters (November–March) see dolphins less frequently, but the Strait of Gibraltar area remains active year-round for the adventurous.

Best Time of Day for Dolphin Sightings

Morning charters between 09:00 and 11:00 offer the calmest seas and best light for photography. Dolphins are often more visible after a night of feeding. Afternoon trips can be equally productive, but the Levante wind picks up around 14:00, making the ride rougher. For the smoothest experience, book a 2-hour or 4-hour slot in the morning.

Which Boat Should You Choose?

Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, just 15–20 minutes by car from Estepona. For small groups (2–5 people), the Dubhe (8 m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4 m, 5 pax) are agile and intimate. For families or groups up to 10, the Azimut 39 (12.5 m, 11 pax) at €749 for 2 hours is a popular choice. Larger parties (up to 12) can opt for the Mangusta 80 (24 m, 12 pax) from €4,719 for 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski—perfect for combining dolphin watching with water sports.

Where Do Dolphins Gather Near Estepona?

Dolphins are most frequently spotted within 3–5 nautical miles of the coast, particularly around the Punta de la Doncella headland and the waters off Cabopino. Skippers also know the zone near the Río Verde estuary, where nutrient-rich currents attract feeding pods. On a 4-hour charter, you can cruise south toward Sotogrande or north toward Cala del Faro, combining dolphin watching with a swim stop.

What’s Included in Your Charter?

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava) and light snacks are provided. No hidden extras—just show up with sunscreen and a camera. For the Mangusta 80 (white or grey), a jet ski is included free on the 4-hour minimum charter, adding a thrill to your dolphin trip.

Tips for a Successful Dolphin-Watching Trip

  • Book a morning slot—calm seas and active dolphins.
  • Bring a camera with a zoom lens—dolphins often approach the bow but can stay 50–100 m away.
  • Wear a light jacket—even in summer, sea breeze can be cool at 20 knots.
  • Don't feed or touch the dolphins—it's illegal and stresses the animals.
  • Choose a boat with a shaded deck—our flybridge yachts like the Azimut 58 Flybridge offer both sun and shade.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best month for dolphin watching in Estepona?

July and August offer the highest sighting rates (often 95%) due to calm seas and abundant fish. May–June and September are also excellent with fewer crowds and still very high success rates.

What time of day is best for dolphin watching?

Morning charters between 9:00 and 11:00 are ideal. The sea is usually calmest then, giving you better visibility and a smoother ride. Dolphins are also more active after feeding overnight.

Which dolphin species can I see near Estepona?

You'll most likely spot bottlenose dolphins, striped dolphins, and common dolphins. Occasionally, pilot whales and even orcas pass through the Strait of Gibraltar area, though sightings are rarer.

How long is a typical dolphin-watching charter from Estepona?

Most charters last 2–4 hours. A 2-hour trip (€749 on Tier A boats) covers the near-coast areas. A 4-hour charter gives you time to reach the best grounds and enjoy a swim stop.

What boats are available for dolphin watching?

From the 5-pax Dubhe or Mariah SX21 for small groups, to the 12-pax Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94 for larger parties. All depart from Puerto Banús, 15–20 minutes from Estepona.

Is dolphin watching guaranteed on an Estepona boat charter?

No, dolphins are wild animals, but sighting rates exceed 90% from May to September. Skippers know the best zones and communicate with other boats to maximise your chances.

What should I bring for a dolphin-watching trip?

Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a light jacket (sea breeze can be cool), and a camera. All charters include water, soft drinks, beer, wine, cava, and light snacks—no need to pack food.

Can I combine dolphin watching with other activities?

Yes. Many charters include a swim stop at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, and you can add jet ski hire (Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski on 4-hour bookings). Snorkelling gear is often available.
